# Dogfood, 2026-10-10: two scenarios on the Darkory repo, through Darkory

The owner (2026-10-10): "Once all done, I want to think about 2 scenarios for this actual Darkory
repo and get it done with this platform too", then "Do all things required. What I need you: for
each requirement, how did it go? Any issue with the current way of the app working? Anything from
UI/UX needs to improve? Put yourself in the user's head and review."

Set-up on the owner's `.dev` Install (never re-initialised; `make dev` started with no browser):
Workspace `darkory` on `/Users/tuongaz/dev/darkory` in `pull_request` mode; Project DARK on the
default Workflows (Implementation, Bug triage) with tuongaz, planner, builder, reviewer, qa and
retro; `triage` granted to planner (the Project's creation made the Skill). Every Step of both
Workflows had a taker; the Install's own `qa` agent takes Verify.

Times are Australia/Sydney; the Install's record is the source (`darkory activity --project DARK`).

| The collapsed state holds while moving between pages in the session | **Met for client-side moves**, which is what a link makes; a hard reload re-expands. The reviewer noted the reload case and that the Task did not ask for it. |
| The page card takes the freed width; nothing else on the bar moves | **Met.** The test asserts the card widens by more than 200px. |
| A Playwright test at 1280 through `[data-sidebar="trigger"]` | **Met.** `web/e2e/sidebar.spec.ts`, one test: collapse, move, restore. |
| `make web-check`, `npm run build`, full Playwright; log as Evidence; a Note saying what changed | **Met.** 1125 unit tests, build, 48 Playwright; the log is Evidence; the Note says what changed and how to see it. builder said "no screenshots/ui-review run": the first look at the control was the reviewer's reading of the diff, and then mine. |

## How the app works: issues found

Ranked by what it costs the owner.

1. **The Shift's ending rules are the same for every Step** (`internal/runner/prompt.go:193-204`: commit; in `pull_request` mode push and open a PR before advancing; attach the test log). A Triage Shift gets "open a PR" beside its Skill's "commit nothing", and the prompt says its own rules win, so planner pushed an empty `dark-2-…` branch. DARK-3, triaged `bug`, at Fix.
2. **Done in `pull_request` mode means "the PR is open", and nothing tells the owner.** DARK-1 went Done at 10:12 and the Inbox stayed "Nothing needs you"; the Task page shows the branch name but no PR; the PR's address lives only inside builder's Note. The human gate the model keeps (the merge) is invisible in the product.
3. **One Shift per agent serialises the Project.** DARK-2 waited three minutes at Code review for the reviewer (the page says "waited 3m", which is good), and now waits at Fix behind DARK-3 because builder took DARK-3 while DARK-2 was blocked. With one builder and one reviewer two Tasks are already a queue. Not a defect; the Agents page should make the queue visible (who waits for whom).
4. **The Runner attaches each Shift's log to the Task as Evidence** (`shift-DARK-2-reviewer-231210.log`, 94.8 kB) beside the Evidence the agent chose (screenshots, test logs). In the Task's record a Shift's log is the Shift's, not the Task's; it doubles the Evidence count on DARK-2 (16) and the Activity lines.
5. **A PR is opened at Build, before any review**, under the owner's GitHub identity (the Runner runs `gh` as the owner). PR #7 and #8 exist for unreviewed work; the reviewer reviews the PR head. That is the `pull_request` mode as designed (ADR 0014/0015), worth saying in the Workspace's words.
6. **A company Skill written for another Project may ride into this one.** The Install's `qa` agent holds `enably-qa` (the Sacca preset's) beside `qa`, and its DARK-3 Note says "enably-qa stack steps do not apply to this repo", which reads as the Shift's prompt carrying another Project's steps into a Darkory Task. One Note is the evidence; how the Runner picks the company Skills for a prompt needs a look before this is called a defect. If it is as the Note says, the prompt should carry only the company Skills that apply to the Task's Project.
7. **Answering a blocking question takes three acts.** "Answer" in the Inbox claims the question and opens its peek, whose only inputs are "Add a Note" and "Complete"; the Complete dialog has a second Note field. The owner has to know that the answer is a Note and that Complete ends it. One box, "Your answer", that writes the Note and completes would do.

## UI/UX, from the owner's head

What I saw walking the pages at 1440 and 390 as tuongaz (screenshots in the session's scratchpad; no page scrolls sideways at 390).

1. **The Inbox is right for questions, silent for merges.** "Needs you 1 · DARK-4 · unblocks DARK-2 · Question from builder · Answer" is exactly the row the owner needs. The same row is owed for "DARK-1 Done · PR #7 awaits your merge", and the Task page's header should carry the PR (number, open/merged) beside the branch.
2. **Agents' Notes and Task bodies are Markdown shown raw.** Backticks and `web/src/app/TopBar.tsx:50` appear as typed; agents write Markdown by habit. Render it (code spans, lists), or tell the agents the record is plain text.
3. **The Workflows list hides its acts.** Four 14px muted icons at the far right of a 1440px row; the owner did not find delete. PR #8 adds the reason when an act is off; the page-level Delete (the ruling) answers the "where" half. Beyond that, the row's acts should read as acts: visible on hover of the row at least, with the ⋯ menu at every width as a fallback.
4. **"lapses in 5m" on a held Task** (the Tasks list, the Agents page) is the heartbeat in jargon. The owner reads "held by builder, working" and wants to know it is alive; "working · 4m" with the lapse only when it is near is enough.
5. **The question's peek shows internals**: "Heartbeat · No expiry", "Session · 1CfsWrR78mb2…". Useful for an agent's Claim, noise on the owner's own.
6. **The Task page's Workflow strip is the best thing on the page**: Triage 6m by PL · Fix 2m by BL · Code review 3m by RV "waited 3m" · Verify · Done, the taken outcomes highlighted, the block drawn ("2m by DARK-4"). Two small things: the "+1" after Triage (a second outcome not drawn) has no explanation, and the "feature → Implementation › Build" chip floats under the strip with nothing tying it to Triage.
7. **Phone: good.** The strip turns vertical, the list groups by Step, the Agents table keeps its columns to Agent · Holds. The Task body's long paragraphs are the heaviest thing on a phone; a "Report" heading over the body would let the strip stay the first screen.
8. **Activity reads as a log, not a story.** "builder attached Evidence … 56.8 kB" ×2, "builder released", "builder added a blocker", "builder filed DARK-4": five rows for one act (asking a question). Group a Shift's end into one row.
9. **Evidence is a list of file names.** DARK-2's twenty screenshots show as links (`03-workflow-page-1280.png`, …) with no preview; the owner opens each in turn to see what the triage saw. Images and small text files should show inline, the log files as a link with their size.
10. **New in this round and right**: the trigger left of the crumbs at every width (PR #7) reads as the kit's control and the collapsed page uses the width; the "Blocked by DARK-4" chip on the list row; "Released" and "Advanced · needs changes" on the Agents page say what each agent did last; and the Task page's **Shift pane** (started 10:20 · Running · tmux dk-DARK-2, the agent's terminal live under the record, with Join) is the one place the owner can watch the work happen without leaving the product. The Workflow's page after the run (Bug triage: a median per Step under its taker, "Done 2 today", "What's happening" listing each Task's path "Triage 5m → Fix 1m → Code review 5m …", and now Delete beside Edit) is the screen that tells the owner how the Workflow performs; it should be where a Project opens.
